description_en: The fortress is located on a rocky spur oriented north-west/south-east, at a few kilometres north-west of Amargadhi, the district headquarter.The site comprises a dozen of structures, including fortification walls and buildings of various shapes. Access to the site is made from the north-east. The entrance is controlled by a quadrangular tower.According to Ram Niwas Pandey the fortress was built by the Doṭiyali king Niraṅjanapāla, also known as Niraipāla, of the Rainka dynasty (Pandey 1997: 171). This king is known from inscriptions dated between 1352 CE and 1362 CE. He also erectedśikharatemples to the east of the fortified area. Niraipāla's time marks the development of the Doṭi kingdom (occupying today's Doti, Baitadi and Dadeldhura districts) as an independant entity from the Khaśa Malla/Yatse empire (12th-14th century). Dilli Raj Sharma reports that the fortress was destroyed in 1685, during a war opposing the kingdom of Doṭi with Kumaon (Sharma 2012: 318-321).The site had at least two phases of occupations, as indicated by the re-used construction material visible in the quadrangular tower (DDL0180-004). Most of the buildings have been dismantled, probably to be re-used for construction by nearby inhabitants. A pedestrian survey allows an outlining of the main structures (see site plan). Likewise, scattered architectural elements suggest the existence of stone pavilions.Structure DDL0180-007 holds a central position. It has a vestibule and thick walls, indicating that it could have been a monument of particular importance.
monument_assessment: Heavily damaged (collapsed, demolished, major cracks and structural damages), Demolition/Dismantling, Collapsed
